title: US Consumer Confidence Analysis — September 2026
discussion_signal: The post distinguishes falling confidence and expectations from continued selective spending, with households prioritizing necessities and reducing some durable purchases. It preserves the important counter-signal that weak sentiment is not identical to an immediate consumption collapse.
linked_research_question: How do current conditions, future expectations, and planned spending diverge when households face inflation, job, and borrowing-cost concerns?
limits: The post interprets a survey release rather than measuring actual future spending
Consumer confidence is not a direct household-income measure
Selective spending patterns may differ across demographic groups
